title: Retail

tables.name: Customers
tables.purpose: One customer can place many orders.

tables.name: Products
tables.purpose: Product catalog and current selling price; order lines retain their historical price.

tables.name: Orders
checks: ParentOrderID IS NULL OR ParentOrderID <> OrderID
tables.purpose: The main business event; linked to its master and optionally to a related earlier event. The parent link is for teaching hierarchy traversal, not a guarantee of an acyclic graph.

tables.name: OrderItems
tables.purpose: Bridge between orders and products; an order can have multiple lines.

tables.name: Payments
tables.purpose: One order can have several payments, or none.

business: Track customers, products, orders, line items and payments. Reconcile line totals and payments without double-counting.

title: Banking / Finance

tables.name: Branches
tables.purpose: A branch services many accounts.

tables.name: Customers
tables.purpose: A customer may own several accounts and loans.

tables.name: Accounts
tables.purpose: Account-level servicing identity; each account belongs to one customer and branch.

tables.name: Transactions
checks: ParentTransactionID IS NULL OR ParentTransactionID <> TransactionID
tables.purpose: The main business event; linked to its master and optionally to a related earlier event. The parent link is for teaching hierarchy traversal, not a guarantee of an acyclic graph.

tables.name: Loans
tables.purpose: Loans reference a borrower and a servicing account; the simplified model permits a different servicing-account owner.

business: Trace transactions to accounts, customers and branches, then summarize lending exposure without multiplying loan balances by transaction counts.

title: Pharma

tables.name: Suppliers
tables.purpose: Each supplier can supply multiple batches.

tables.name: Products
tables.purpose: A product can be manufactured in many batches.

tables.name: Warehouses
tables.purpose: Locations holding stock from several batches.

tables.name: Batches
checks: ParentBatchID IS NULL OR ParentBatchID <> BatchID
tables.purpose: The main business event; linked to its master and optionally to a related earlier event. The parent link is for teaching hierarchy traversal, not a guarantee of an acyclic graph.

tables.name: Inventory
tables.purpose: Bridge between batches and warehouses; one row per batch/location.

business: Track product batches from suppliers to warehouse stock. Identify unstocked batches and zero-stock locations.

title: Healthcare

tables.name: Patients
tables.purpose: Synthetic patients; one patient may have several encounters.

tables.name: Doctors
tables.purpose: One doctor is assigned to each encounter in this simplified teaching model.

tables.name: Medications
tables.purpose: Synthetic catalog for relational practice; no clinical dosing guidance.

tables.name: Encounters
checks: ParentEncounterID IS NULL OR ParentEncounterID <> EncounterID
tables.purpose: The main business event; linked to its master and optionally to a related earlier event. The parent link is for teaching hierarchy traversal, not a guarantee of an acyclic graph.

tables.name: Prescriptions
tables.purpose: A prescription links one encounter to one medication; multiple prescriptions may belong to an encounter.

business: Follow patients through encounters with doctors and medications prescribed. Report encounters without prescriptions and avoid repeated encounter charges.

title: Oil

tables.name: Sites
tables.purpose: Origin sites dispatch many shipments.

tables.name: Carriers
tables.purpose: Each shipment is assigned to one carrier.

tables.name: Products
tables.purpose: Product catalog; shipment lines retain historical unit prices.

tables.name: Shipments
checks: ParentShipmentID IS NULL OR ParentShipmentID <> ShipmentID
tables.purpose: The main business event; linked to its master and optionally to a related earlier event. The parent link is for teaching hierarchy traversal, not a guarantee of an acyclic graph.

tables.name: ShipmentItems
tables.purpose: Bridge between shipments and oil products; one row per shipment/product combination.

business: Track origin sites, carriers, shipments and product lines; reconcile shipment values and identify missing detail.

title: Retail Supply Chain

tables.name: Warehouses
tables.purpose: Fulfillment centers and store depots; each warehouse has stock movements and balances and receives private label production.

tables.name: Suppliers
tables.purpose: Where stock comes from. Supplier 4 is the in-house Private Label plant, the source of every Made product.

tables.name: Products
tables.purpose: One catalog: Bought products come from outside suppliers; Made products are produced in the Private Label plant from a recipe.

tables.name: Materials
tables.purpose: Raw materials for Made products. Quantities are in the material-specific unit.

tables.name: BillOfMaterials
tables.purpose: Recipe bridge: one row per Made product and required material, per unit produced.

tables.name: ProductionOrders
checks: CompletedDate IS NULL OR CompletedDate >= StartDate
tables.purpose: Factory runs for Made products. PlannedCost is the recipe material cost; finished units are received into WarehouseID.

tables.name: MaterialUsage
tables.purpose: Actual material consumed per production order and material; compare it with the recipe.

tables.name: StockMovements
checks: ParentMovementID IS NULL OR ParentMovementID <> MovementID
tables.purpose: The main business event; linked to its master and optionally to a related earlier event. The parent link is for teaching hierarchy traversal, not a guarantee of an acyclic graph.

tables.name: StockBalances
tables.purpose: One snapshot per warehouse and product: opening stock plus the signed seed movements equals QuantityOnHand. No trigger updates it automatically.

business: Buy or make products, move stock through warehouses, and reconcile production, receipts, dispatches and balances.

title: Retail Logistics

tables.name: Customers
tables.purpose: Customers request retail deliveries; one customer may have many shipments.

tables.name: Carriers
tables.purpose: Delivery partners; each shipment is assigned to one carrier.

tables.name: Shipments
checks: ParentShipmentID IS NULL OR ParentShipmentID <> ShipmentID
tables.purpose: The main business event; linked to its master and optionally to a related earlier event. The parent link is for teaching hierarchy traversal, not a guarantee of an acyclic graph.

tables.name: ShipmentPackages
tables.purpose: Physical parcels with individual tracking numbers and promised delivery dates.

tables.name: TrackingEvents
tables.purpose: Append-only package scan history; select the latest scan rather than counting it as another package.

business: Follow customer shipments through carriers, parcels and tracking events. Find missing scans and late deliveries without multiplying freight charges.

title: E-commerce

tables.name: Customers
tables.purpose: Shoppers; one customer can place many orders, and heavy buyers order almost every week.

tables.name: Sellers
tables.purpose: Third-party sellers; each sells in one department and fulfils its own orders.

tables.name: Products
tables.purpose: Catalog listing price; the price actually charged is kept on each order item.

tables.name: Orders
checks: ParentOrderID IS NULL OR ParentOrderID <> OrderID
tables.purpose: The main business event; linked to its master and optionally to a related earlier event. The parent link is for teaching hierarchy traversal, not a guarantee of an acyclic graph.

tables.name: OrderItems
tables.purpose: Lines of an order; UnitPrice is the price charged, after any deal discount.

tables.name: Payments
tables.purpose: Payments per order: an order can be split between a gift card and a card, or be unpaid.

business: Run a marketplace with tens of thousands of orders a year: daily volume, sellers, order lines and split payments, reconciled without double-counting.

title: Brokerage

tables.name: Clients
tables.purpose: Synthetic individual brokerage clients; each can hold multiple accounts.

tables.name: Securities
tables.purpose: Fictitious stock and ETF instruments with unique symbols.

tables.name: BrokerageAccounts
tables.purpose: Each brokerage account belongs to one client; Region is the servicing region.

tables.name: TradeOrders
checks: ParentOrderID IS NULL OR ParentOrderID <> OrderID
tables.purpose: The main business event; linked to its master and optionally to a related earlier event. The parent link is for teaching hierarchy traversal, not a guarantee of an acyclic graph.

tables.name: Executions
tables.purpose: Individual partial fills. Total fills must not exceed the requested order quantity; this cross-row rule is validated by reconciliation.

business: Trace clients and accounts through securities, trade orders and partial executions. Reconcile filled quantities and weighted average execution prices.
source_note: An independent, synthetic brokerage training model. Scope: buy orders for fictitious stocks and ETFs, including partial fills. Settlement, cash ledgers, positions, margin, taxes and options are outside this five-table model. WorkflowStatus is an administrative practice flag; derive fill status from requested and executed quantities.
